title: docs(fields,roadmap): the built-in locale count is ten, and the shipped docblock stops restating it
body:
Fixes #9615

Clause-②: no

`@object-ui/i18n` ships **ten** built-in locale packs. Seven sites in this tree said eleven,
and one of them is published source.

## The count, enumerated rather than trusted

The card states the shipped count as ten. That number was re-derived here rather than adopted:
`readme-locale-count-7989.test.ts` runs both published doors and asserts they agree —
`BUILT_IN_LANGUAGE_CODES` from the package entry, and the `builtInLocales` map behind the
`@object-ui/i18n/locales` subpath. Run at this branch's head, it passes: **4 tests, 1 file**.
The codes are `en zh ja ko de fr es pt ru ar`. Deliberately NOT counted by listing
`src/locales/*.ts`: that directory holds thirteen files and three of them are not packs, which
is the very miscount this card is about — the 7989 pin says so in its own header.

## My census differs from the card's, and the difference is the card's own premise moving

Re-run at my head, not adopted:

| reading | card | measured here | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| sites | 9 over 3 files | **7 over 2 files** | the 2 `packages/i18n/README.md` sites are already repaired |
| lit control | exactly 3 files carry the string | **2 files** | same cause |
| negative control `99 built-in locales` | 0 | **0** | agrees |

objectui#7989 is closed; its repair landed as `e1c27e49`. So what this card carries is not "seven
more besides that one" — it is the whole live population of the wrong count. The triage comment
read the same thing.

### A blind spot in the instrument, reported and not swept

The census pattern matches a bare numeral followed by whitespace. Run bold-tolerant at the same
merge-base it reads **9 sites over 4 files**, not 7 over 2. The two extra are
`.changeset/7989-i18n-readme-locale-count.md` and the 7989 pin's own docblock, both of which
write the numeral bolded and both of which describe the defect in the PAST TENSE. They are
historical record, not live claims, so they are correctly out of scope — but the card's lit
control ("exactly three files carry the string") was taken with a bold-blind instrument and
therefore under-counted its own population. Widening the census is not this card; the reading is
recorded so the next seat does not take that control as complete.

## What changed

**`packages/fields/src/widgets/file-size-guard.ts` — published source.** The docblock asserted
the shared `fields.file.exceedsMaxSize` key was "already translated in all 11 built-in locales".
Measured, not assumed, that this actually ships: after building the package, the docblock's text
is present in `dist/widgets/file-size-guard.d.ts`, which is in this package's `files` — so the
false count went out in every tarball and is what a consumer's editor shows on hover. Positive
controls `exceedsMaxSize` and `maxSizeError` both fire in the same grep.

⭐ The number is **removed**, not corrected. Correcting it to ten reproduces the construct that
permitted the error, and this repository has now watched that construct recur three times over
this one fact: objectui#3351 in a changeset file, objectui#7989 in the i18n README, this one in
shipped source. The sentence now claims only what it needs — the key is translated in every
locale the package ships — and names `all-locales-key-parity.test.ts` as the instrument that
re-derives it. That test asserts the stronger invariant (every pack defines every `en` key) over
whatever the pack set is on the day it runs, so an eleventh pack makes the sentence MORE true
rather than false. There is no figure left to rot, which is AGENTS.md commandment #9 applied
rather than restated. The key is in fact present in all ten packs today, checked pack by pack
with a negative control.

⚠️ This is why no new pin is added here. The 7989 precedent pinned its README because its repair
left a corrected NUMBER in the prose; this repair leaves no number, so there is nothing for a pin
to compare. If a reviewer wants the stricter shape — a pin asserting this docblock never regains a
hardcoded count — say so and it is a small follow-up.

**`ROADMAP.md` — six sites, prose, no new mechanism.** Per the dispatch, a roadmap gets the
correct number and the arithmetic error, not a mechanism. `ROADMAP.md` line 632 carried the
arithmetic that manufactured the eleven: its list read `(en, zh, ja, de, fr, es, ar, ru, pt, ko, + ar)`
— eleven entries, ten unique, `ar` counted once in the list and once as the suffix. The duplicate is
removed, not merely the number corrected, so the next enumerator does not recount it. The three
sibling lines each claimed eleven while enumerating ten codes ON THE SAME LINE. Ten is already the
house convention in that document, which states "all 10 locales" at eight other sites.

No line numbers move: `ROADMAP.md` is 1899 lines before and after. Nothing in the tree cites a line
address into either changed file, checked both directions.

## Changeset

`patch` on `@object-ui/fields`, matching objectui#7989's own `patch` on `@object-ui/i18n` for the
same class of defect on the same kind of surface. The reason is measured, not conventional: the
docblock reaches `dist/*.d.ts`, and `dist` is in this package's `files`, so a published byte moved.
`check-changeset-presence.mjs` classifies the diff the same way — "1 of them published source of a
package the release covers".

## Verification

Every exit code below was captured before any pipe.

| what | result |
|---|---|
| `vitest run packages/fields/` + the two cited i18n instruments | **168 files, 2908 tests, all passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, both echoed) |
| `@object-ui/fields` dependency-closure build | exit 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0, 7937 files |
| `check:new-line-citations` | exit 0, **0 new citations** |
| `check:changeset-claims` | exit 0, corpus 1 changeset |
| `check:i18n-keys` · `check:i18n-drift` | exit 0 · exit 0, "0 en value(s) changed" |
| `docs:check-links` | exit 0, 17 scan roots |
| `check:comment-mask-corpus` | exit 0, residue unchanged at its ceiling |
| `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check-changeset-presence` | exit 0 · exit 0 |

The test-file arithmetic is stated because a filtered run that silently matches nothing also reads
green: `packages/fields` holds 166 test files, plus the 2 i18n instruments this branch's comment
now cites, which is the 168 vitest reported. Both cited instruments therefore really ran.

`check:doc-snippets` returned **exit 2 — "could not run"**, which is NOT MEASURED, not a failure: it
needs a scoped 34-package build first. Narrowed away with proof rather than skipped — that gate
type-checks fenced snippets, and this diff changes none. All six edited `ROADMAP.md` lines are
outside code fences (checked with a fence-state walk), the changeset has zero fences, and the
TypeScript diff is comment-only: 19 changed lines, 0 of them non-comment, with a classifier proven
able to fire on a known code line.

`pnpm lint` is a repository-wide scan that belongs to CI. The narrowed run is declared with its three
readings: the population comes from the config's own `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']`; the run reports
**1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings** from `--format json`; and the invariance holds because
`eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions.project`),
so a comment-only edit in one file cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The same command was
shown able to report a finding, on a control file created inside the tree and removed with cleanup
verified by observing state rather than by reading an exit code.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, noted and NOT filed:

- `packages/i18n/src/index.ts` and `packages/i18n/package.json` both hedge "10+" where the figure is
  exactly ten. The card excludes both on purpose and objectui#7989's ruling protects them as
  already-correct. A hedge on an exact number is a weaker defect than a wrong one. Successor: the
  next card that touches the i18n package description.
- `ROADMAP.md`'s locale counts stay RESTATED rather than derived. That is the dispatch's explicit
  boundary for a planning document, not an oversight. Successor: none — nothing re-derives a
  roadmap, and nothing should.
- The plain-text census under-counts by missing bolded numerals, measured above. Successor: whoever
  next runs a figure census in this repository; the reading is recorded here rather than filed
  because the sites it newly finds are historical records that want no repair.
